title: On‑Prem CI/CD Orchestration Checklist and Signal Flows
content:
Purpose
This is a working checklist + signal flow guide for orchestrating CI/CD and releases for private (VPC / on‑prem) Redwood deployments. It focuses on Helms/Argo driven delivery, Terraform module contract boundaries, image signing & attestation, and deterministic rollback triggers.

Context / Assumptions
- Target environments: customer VPC (single-tenant) and on‑prem appliance clusters (RKE/k8s 1.25+).
- We gate upgrades through our GitOps control plane (ArgoCD + optional Argo Rollouts).
- Images are signed with our CI signing key and an attestation attached (slsa predicate + digest).
- Terraform modules provision infra + k8s bootstrap; CI does not mutate infra during chart upgrades.

High level phases
1) Developer CI -> build/test + sign image + publish SBOM/attestation
2) Merge -> GitOps commit to customer repo or our private deploy repo (depending on flow)
3) ArgoCD detects change -> preflight checks (k8s, CRDs, quotas) -> create canary workload
4) Canary evaluation window (metrics + smoke) -> promote to bulk rollout if pass
5) Post-rollout verification -> traffic routing cutover -> cleanup canaries & cache warm
6) Observability & postmortem triggers on anomalies

Preflight checklist (CI / CD job level)
- Static checks: Helm lint exit 0, charts pass schema tests, values schema validated against customer constraints.
- Terraform plan: module inputs validated, plan output saved as artifact; if plan changes network or IAM, mark manual approval required.
- Images: container digest recorded, SBOM published to artifacts store, signature present and verifiable with public key.
- Attestation: slsa predicate containing SOURCE_REPO, COMMIT_SHA, BUILDER_ID, SBOM_URL, DIGEST.
- Compatibility matrix check: ensure model runtime and runtime flags match pinned runtime in customer config (quantization/FP flags).

Terraform module notes (interface and safety guards)
- Module: private_deploy.k8s_cluster (vX.Y)
  - inputs (string): cluster_name, control_plane_cidr, node_pool_count, allowed_ecr_accounts
  - outputs (list): kubeconfig_secret_name, node_pool_ids
  - safety: any change to control_plane_cidr or allowed_ecr_accounts requires manual apply with TF_MANUAL=true and an approval ticket (jira:PD-XXXX).
- Module: private_deploy.image_policy
  - inputs: signing_public_key_kid, allowed_signers (list), attestation_enabled (bool)
  - contract: ArgoCD admission webhook will refuse images whose digest is not in signed artifacts list.
- Recommendation: keep infra modules separate from releases; release pipeline should never run terraform apply on customer infra except for explicit infra change releases.

Argo + Helm release flow (practical steps)
- CI builds and tags image: registry/customer/infra-service:sha-<short>
- CI job posts a release manifest to artifacts/ (helm-values-<sha>.yaml) and pushes git tag + PR to the repo that Argo tracks.
- ArgoCD detects PR merge -> sync begins. Use hooks: preSync -> run preflight Job (short smoke & kube checks).
- For canaries: annotate HelmRelease (or kustomize) with rollout.strategy=canary; Argo Rollouts handles shifting weights.
- Example canary schedule:
  - 0–5m: 5% traffic, smoke test (liveness, readiness probes, basic token generation)
  - 5–20m: 25% traffic, latency p50/p95 within 1.5x baseline, error_rate < 0.5% of baseline
  - 20–60m: 100% traffic (if previous checks pass)
- On success: annotate release with rollout.state=promoted and let garbage collector cleanup canary resources.

Signal definitions (deterministic gating)
- Success signals (combined):
  - Smoke check pass (synthetic request/response validation) — must be green for 3 consecutive runs.
  - SLO health: p95 latency <= baseline * 1.5 AND error_rate <= baseline + 0.5% (rolling 5m windows).
  - Resource stability: pods restart_count delta < 2 in 10m window, CPU and mem within expected headroom.
  - Model quality quick-checks: sample inference on canary model with known prompts; similarity metrics within configured thresholds.
- Failure signals (auto-trigger rollback):
  - Critical errors: >1 elevated crashloop backoff in 5m OR pod OOMKilled >0 during canary.
  - Latency spike: p95 > 2x baseline for >3 consecutive 1m windows.
  - Error spike: 5xx rate > baseline + 2% for >2 minutes.
  - Attestation mismatch: digest used by runtime != signed digest from artifact store.
- Decision rules: any single critical failure -> immediate rollback. Non‑critical anomalies -> pause rollout, notify oncall, run extended checks.

Rollback mechanics (automated + manual)
- Automated rollback path (Argo Rollouts + operator):
  - Argo detects rollout failure -> switches traffic back to previous ReplicaSet; HelmReleases are reconciled to previous commit.
  - CI posts a rollback artifact: rollback-trigger.json with failing release SHA, failing metrics snapshot, and recommended revert commit.
- Manual emergency rollback script (ops):
  - ./scripts/trigger-rollback.sh --env prod --release <name> --target-sha <previous_sha>
  - Internals: script opens a rollback jira ticket, tags commit in gitops repo, forces Argo sync with --prune=false to avoid tearing down shared resources.

Image signing and attestation checklist
- Signing key management: CI holds ephemeral signing key; a KMS/HSM root signs CI key periodically. Rotate keys quarterly.
- SBOM: SPDX v2.2 output stored at artifacts/sbom/<digest>.spdx.json.
- Attestation contents: builder id, commit sha, build timestamp, sbom url, digest algorithm, predicate. Store attestations in the registry (OCI attestation) and in artifact storage.
- Admission webhook: verify signature OR verify attestation predicate links to known CI run. Log mismatch to audit log and create PD ticket automatically.

Post-rollout verification (10–60m window)
- Run a smoke harness that exercises common paths: short chat generation, streaming client handshake, KV cache performance check. Capture latencies and success rates.
- Run a synthetic load test at 1.1x typical tps for 5m to validate resource headroom.
- Warm caches: call warm-up endpoint for hot prompt sets (configurable list per customer).

Observability and dashboards (what to watch)
- Dashboards: per-release p50/p95 latency, request success rate, token/sec, CPU/mem headroom, pod restarts.
- Alerts to tie to rollout automation: any alert triggered by the canary namespace should be annotated with rollout_id and must surface on the rollout channel.
- Logging: structured fields: rollout_id, image_digest, commit_sha, canary_weight. Capture combined logs to the release artifact store for postmortem.

Testing and validation matrix (to include in CI)
- Helm/Template unit tests: chart unit validation with randomized values (fuzz) for common knobs.
- Integration smoke: deploy to ephemeral k8s cluster (kinD) with disabling heavy components; run basic inference path.
- Contract tests: ensure CRD versions match operator expectations; if CRD version bumps, block rollout until operator upgrade plan is applied.

Open items / TODOs
- Define exact thresholds for model quality quick-checks per model family (Priya to draft).
- Add terraform guardrail to prevent accidental change to subnet allocation during rollout pipeline (Daniel to implement).
- Build a CLI that surface attestations for a given digest (Evan exploring implementation).

Appendix: quick command snippets
- Verify attestation locally:
  cosign verify-attestation --key kms://projects/redwood/keys/ci-signing-key \
    --predicate predicate.json registry/customer/infra-service@sha256:<digest>

- Force Argo sync after PR revert:
  kubectl -n argocd exec deploy/argocd-repo-server -- argocd repo sync <app-name> --revision <commit> --force

- Emergency rollback (manual):
  ./scripts/trigger-rollback.sh --env prod --release infra-service --target-sha abc1234 --create-ticket

Notes on being conservative
- Err on the side of manual approval for infra-changing terraform plans.
- Prefer smaller canaries with longer candidate evaluation for model-serving changes vs UI-only changes.
- Keep image-signing verification in the admission path; do not rely purely on Argo annotations.

If we adopt this we should iterate over one real customer upgrade window and capture signal tuning values. This doc is intentionally prescriptive on flows and permissive on thresholds — please annotate with concrete numbers from field runs.
